title: React Architecture Core Check
description: Check your understanding of project structure, feature architecture, separation of concerns, patterns, scalable state, and error boundaries.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is the recommended approach when a React project is still small?

options.text: Start with a deeply nested enterprise folder layout
Keep the structure simple and let real pain points guide growth
Move every component into a global shared folder
Create a separate package for every component

questions.explanation: The architecture lessons emphasize starting simple and adding structure when the current layout starts to hurt.

questions.prompt: In a feature-based architecture, what should a feature folder usually contain?

options.text: Only CSS files
Only route components
UI, hooks, API code, and tests owned by that feature
All shared utilities used by the whole app

questions.explanation: Feature folders group code by product capability and ownership, not just by technical file type.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a feature public API file such as an index export?

options.text: Expose every internal helper to other features
Make imports longer but more explicit
Define the supported imports other modules may depend on
Disable tree shaking

questions.explanation: A public API creates an import boundary so other features rely only on intentional exports.

questions.prompt: Which are examples of separate concerns in a React app? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Rendering UI
Fetching data
Domain calculations
Duplicating server state into several components

questions.explanation: UI rendering, data access, and domain rules are different concerns. Duplicated state is a design problem, not a concern to preserve.

questions.prompt: Why are custom hooks useful for architecture?

options.text: They let components share stateful logic without mixing it into presentation code
They replace all components
They make Hooks optional
They prevent all re-renders

questions.explanation: Custom hooks are a common way to separate reusable stateful behavior from component markup.

questions.prompt: Which design pattern lets related components share implicit parent context, such as Tabs, TabList, and TabPanel?

options.text: Adapter pattern
Compound components
Singleton pattern
Observer pattern only

questions.explanation: Compound components coordinate related children through a parent component API.

questions.prompt: What is the default state architecture guideline from the module?

options.text: Put all state in a global store immediately
Keep state close to where it is used until sharing needs justify moving it
Store all state in URL parameters
Avoid reducers in every case

questions.explanation: Keeping state close reduces accidental coupling and unnecessary app-wide re-renders.

questions.prompt: Which errors can a React error boundary catch? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Errors thrown during rendering below the boundary
Errors thrown in lifecycle methods below the boundary
Errors thrown inside an event handler callback
Errors from asynchronous code after the render finished

questions.explanation: Error boundaries catch render and lifecycle failures in their subtree, but not event handler or later async errors.
